scope: Two Fells Point guides and the Domino Sugar record that shares the incorrect Rash Field camera coordinate. Other Blueway guides are not certified by this review.

decisions.tripValue: The steward names a distinct Canton waterfront trail connecting Canton Waterfront Park and Fells Point. It is not interchangeable with the Inner Harbor perimeter simply because both finish at Bond Street Wharf.
decisions.sourceDistance: The steward publishes 1.3 miles one way; its linked AllTrails route lists a 2.7-mile out-and-back. Clarify the return rather than treating 1.3 miles as the total return journey.
decisions.coordinateCorrection: Replace the Fells Point camera center at 39.2804218,-76.6289316 with the manager-linked place anchor at 39.2804218,-76.5939127. The current dock-owner page expressly permits public recreational access and describes the boardwalk/gangway approach.
decisions.geometry: Replace the line extending west through the city with a generalized waterfront route past the Canton marinas, ending at the Fells dock-area anchor. About 1.33 mapped miles; the steward's 1.3-mile planning distance remains the source value.

decisions.tripValue: The steward names an Inner Harbor, Harbor East and Harbor Point perimeter itinerary with different shoreline commitments from Canton. Keep its independent guide and public launch pair.
decisions.sourceDistance: The current page body publishes about two miles between the Inner Harbor and Fells Point launches. Its page title says 2.5 miles; use the route body and identify the distance as an approximate one-way itinerary. The return is additional, roughly four miles overall.
decisions.coordinateCorrection: Correct the shared Fells anchor. The Rash Field value was also a linked map camera center; the linked entity is a park centroid rather than the launch. Use an approximate northeast shoreline/dock-area anchor at 39.28208,-76.6084, interpreted from the publisher-linked map, documented northeast-park approach by Rusty Scupper, and hydrography. This is an access-area estimate with approximately 150 feet of location uncertainty, not a surveyed gangway or water entry. Check the actual dock and waterline on site.
decisions.geometry: Generalized shoreline planning line through the Inner Harbor and around Harbor Point, approximately 1.79 drawn miles. It simplifies the publisher's roughly two-mile perimeter and pier approaches; it is not a GPS navigation track. Do not inflate the line to manufacture agreement with a published distance.
decisions.sourceLimits: The dock owner's Inner Harbor page retains an anticipated June opening and an unrelated Annapolis map embed. Those are not used as current opening-date or coordinate proof. The current Blueway launch directory identifies the public launch; the owner describes its northeast Rash Field approach. Older aerial imagery does not establish the present floating-dock outline.

decisions.finding: The existing record promises a 1.6-mile Rash Field return loop, using the same camera-center launch and a line through the northern harbor. The current steward page names Rash Field and Hull Street Pier, and its linked map explicitly lists 1.6 miles point-to-point along the southern shoreline. The page body also says 1.3 miles, conflicting with the headline. The current loop does not implement the documented itinerary.
decisions.missingEvidence: An exact current Hull Street kayak landing, approach and public water-access terms, the complete point-to-point line and crossing exposure, and an explicit shuttle or return plan. A city pedestrian easement/fishing pier and proximity to water are not proof of a usable kayak landing.
decisions.preservation: Preserve the existing source itinerary, hazards, citations and legacy asset for correction. Apply the shared Rash Field dock-area anchor to its stored endpoints for registry consistency; the original camera coordinates remain recorded here and recoverable at base commit 428e52eda54db0f049d0eb784ae918d41643564a. Keep the unsupported loop out of public guides, catalog, Explore and sitemap; do not redirect it to a different trail.

geometryValidation.method: Visually compare the generalized itinerary with the steward-embedded maps and sample each candidate segment every five meters against the downloaded USGS NHD waterbody footprint. This is a land-crossing screen, not a current navigation, traffic, depth, ownership or access certification.
geometryValidation.innerHarbor: 591 samples within the generalized water footprint.
geometryValidation.canton: Four initial samples outside the generalized water footprint, limited to the first approximately 15 meters at the DNR-mapped public boat-ramp anchor. The subsequent shoreline route samples are in water.
geometryValidation.limitations: USGS hydrography is generalized and can omit recent dock construction. The attempted NHDArea query timed out; no area-layer completeness claim is made. The old city water endpoint was unavailable. Neither missing source is treated as a clean validation.
geometryValidation.userFacingQualification: The two reviewed geometry features carry an explicit generalized-planning flag. Their route maps display a shoreline-planning caption, and GPX metadata plus track descriptions carry the same qualification. Other unflagged maps and GPX descriptions are unchanged.

invariants: Both corrected guides remain planning-only with the same upstream USGS proxy and NOAA tide context; no numeric paddle cutoff is introduced.
Other route records, gauge assignments, scoring rules and original consolidation-pilot choices remain unchanged.
No source or map check in this batch establishes Google ranking recovery.

localValidation.indexabilityAudit: passed with no errors or warnings
